description: On 11 April 2025, the FISHING VESSEL "FUNDY TRAPPER II", with 4 persons onboard, became disabled due to a rope in the propeller.  The vessel was towed to Yarmouth, N.S. by the FISHING VESSEL " SEAS N AIR 2012.
On 10 April 2025, the FISHING VESSEL "L'ACADJONNE", with 3 people onboard, experienced a propeller failure.  The vessel was towed to Cape St. Mary's , N.S. by the CCGS SAMBRO.
On 10 April 2025, the FISHING VESSEL "JESS & JAN" with 3 persons onboard, experienced a main engine failure. The vessel was towed to West Head, N.S. by the CCGS CHEDABUCTO BAY.
On 09 April 2025, the ferry RO-RO "FELIX-ANTOINE-SAVARD", waiting for 1808
On 09 April 2025, the cargo vessel "CTMA VOYAGEUR 2", awaiting 1808.

On 09 April 2025, the bulk carrier "CSL NIAGARA", reported having struck the lower wall of lock number 3 located in Beauharnois, QC while transiting the seaway upbound. The vessel anchored to assess the damages, major damage to the forepeak ballast tank was reported.
On 08 April 2025, the FISHING "SAMANTHA NATHAN", SUSTAINS DAMAGE RENDER UNSEAWORTHY/UNFIT FOR PURPOSE - Unfit for purpose - ice, weather, etc..
On 08 April 2025, the FISHING "TURMEL B.", TOTAL FAILURE OF ANY MACHINERY OR TECHNICAL SYSTEM.

On 05 April 2025, the fishing vessel "BIBIANNE MARIE II", with 6 people on board, reported being disabled with transmission issues in the vicinity of Baie des Chaleurs, NB. The vessel was towed to Caraquet, NB by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CASCUMPEC BAY".

On 07 April 2025, the fishing vessel "SCOUT SWIMMER", with 5 people on board, reported having issues with their engine in the Gulf off St. Lawrence off of Le Goulet. The vessel was initially towed toward Shippegan, NB by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "KOPIT HOPSON" while carrying out minor repairs. Later, the tow was discontinued, and the vessel proceeded under its own power to the wharf.

On 30 March 2025, the tanker "JOHNNY RANGER", while under the conduct of a pilot, reported having sustained an engine failure during a manoeuvre between sections No. 102 and 103 of Port de Montréal, QC. The vessel was anchored off Pointe-aux-Trembles, QC where the crew effected repairs before resuming the voyage.

On 05 April 2025, the fishing vessel "2ND WIND IV", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with engine issues in the Bay of Fundy off Long Island. The vessel was towed to Westport, NS by another fishing vessel.

On 31 March 2025, the ferry "WOLFE ISLANDER III", with 35 people on board, reported having struck a mooring dolphin while berthing at Wolfe Island's Dawson Point, ON. The vessel was secured, and the crew assessed the damages.
On 28 March 2025, the MV "MACCOA" lost engine power while approaching lock 3 at Beauharnois. The vessel was repaired and underway on March 29.

On 28 March 2025, the tanker "JOHNNY RANGER", while under the conduct of a pilot, reported having sustained an engine failure at the approach of an anchorage off Pointe-aux-Trembles, QC. The vessel was anchored and the crew effected repairs.

On 27 March 2025, the hovercraft CCGS "SIPU MUIN" reported damage to the port propulsion motor rendering the vessel non-operational. The damage was repaired and the vessel was repaired and  returned to service on 31 March.

On 06 April 2025, the fishing vessel "UNCLE RODDIE GOULD", with 7 people on board, reported being disabled with engine issues off Louisbourg, NS. The vessel was towed to Louisbourg, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "LA POILE BAY".

On 04 April 2025, the fishing vessel "LADY EILEEN" reported having sustained the total failure of their propulsion system while departing Sambro, NS. The vessel was towed back to Sambro by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "HARE BAY".
On 07 April 2025, the FISHING "CINDY MAXIME", TOTAL FAILURE OF ANY MACHINERY OR TECHNICAL SYSTEM.
On 05 April 2025, the FISHING "MANON YVON", TOTAL FAILURE OF ANY MACHINERY OR TECHNICAL SYSTEM.

On 28 March 2025, the fishing vessel "THOMIKA", with 5 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure in the Gulf of St. Lawrence off Île d'Entrée, QC. The vessel was towed to Cap-aux-Meules, QC by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "BAIE DE PLAISANCE".
On 05 April 2025, the FISHING "OCEANOS", STRIKING - Allision with a fixed object (striking - includes berthed/docked vessels).
On 05 April 2025, the CARGO - SOLID "ALGOMA SAULT", RISK OF COLLISION (near collision) - With another vessel or other floating object.
On 28 March 2025, the fishing vessel "MERIDIAN 66" ran aground within the harbour limits of Rivière-au-Renard, QC. The fishing vessel was freed by a vessel of opportunity.

On 02 April 2025, the TUG "MOLLY M I" sustained an engine failure while towing the barge "GLOVERTOWN SPIRIT" on the St. Lawrence River, near Champlain, Quebec.  The vessel anchored and carried out repairs before resuming its intended voyage.

On 31 March 2025, the pilot boat "PACIFIC GUARDIAN" reported having made contact with the flare of the stern of the "MV EASTERN BIRDIE" after pilot boarding in Juan de Fuca Strait off Vancouver, BC. The pilot boat sustained minor damage to its mast; no damage to the tanker was reported.

On 01 April 2025, the tug "INLET CRUSADER" reported having run aground and taking on water in Collingwood Channel, BC. The crew monitored the damaged void space while proceeding to a shipyard in Richmond, BC using its port engine.

On 01 April 2025, the fishing vessel "KNOT GUILTY", with 4 people on board, reported being disabled with engine issues in the Bay of Fundy. The fishing vessel "GRACE ABOUNDS" towed the vessel to Ingalls Head, NB.

On 30 March 2025, the fishing vessel "WHITETAIL 15", with 6 people on board, reported being disabled with engine issues east of Cape Breton, NS. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "LA POILE BAY" towed the vessel to Louisbourg.

On 09 March 2025, the fishing vessel "C32734BC" known as "GWI GWI", with 1 person on board, reported having run aground with its crew member injured in Goletas Channel off Doyle Island, BC. The disabled vessel was anchored on scene by the crew of the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "PACHENA BAY", that also transported the injured crew member to Port Hardy, BC to meet with an ambulance.

On 28 March 2025, the passenger vessel "STHUQI'", with 157 people on board, reported having collided with a log and sustained a water ingress in English Bay, BC. The vessel proceeded to a wharf in Vancouver, BC and the crew assessed the damages.

On 30 March 2025, the fishing vessel "ARNOLD EDWARD", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure in the Gulf of Maine off Yarmouth, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SAMBRO".

On 27 March 2025, the fishing vessel, "PIELAW", with 4 people on board, reported being disabled due to a loss of steering in the Bay of Fundy. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SHEDIAC BAY" towed the vessel to Dipper Harbour, NB.

On 26 March 2025, the unregistered fishing vessel "KYLE SEA XVI", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure in the vicinity of St. Marys Bay, NS. The vessel was towed to Meteghan, NS, by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SAMBRO".

On 27 March 2025, the bulk carrier "CHARALAMBOS", while under the conduct of a pilot, reported having sustained a steering system failure in English Bay, BC. The vessel proceeded to an anchorage to assess the issue.

On 24 March 2025, the fishing vessel "F.F.S.", with 2 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure off Baccaro, NS. The vessel was towed to West Head, NS, by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 23 March 2025, the fishing vessel "AQUA JEWEL", with 3 people on board, reported a loss of electrical power and communications in the vicinity of Long Island Bay, NB. The vessel proceeded to North Head, NB, for repairs.

On 21 March 2025, the fishing vessel "NICOLE AND SISTERS II", with 2 people on board, reported being disabled off Port La Tour, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 20 March 2025, the unregistered fishing vessel "BIG JIM", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a fouled propeller off Woods Harbour, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 20 March 2025, the unregistered fishing vessel "HIT N MISS I", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure off Woods Harbour, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".
On 24 March 2025, the fishing vessel "JUDY J V", with 4 people on board, reported being disabled off Tofino, BC. The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPE ANN" towed the "JUDY J V" to a dock in Tofino.

On 14 March 2025, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "MAMILOSSA", with 5 people on board, reported having sustained a total failure of its steering gear system while de-icing on Lac Saint-Pierre, QC. The vessel returned to its base in Trois-Rivières, QC, to conduct repairs.

On 24 March 2025, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "VINCENT MASSEY" reported having fouled its starboard propeller with the anchor chain for a buoy while performing aids to navigation service near Portneuf, QC. The vessel proceeded to Québec, QC, using its port engine.

On 22 March 2025, the TUG "CAPTAIN COOK", with the loaded barge "M8005" in tow, reported being disabled due to main engine fuel system problem while transiting off Merry Island, BC. The tug "NORTH ARM VICTOR" took over "CAPTAIN COOK" and the tug "JOSE NARVAEZ" took over the barge "M8005", and both tugs proceeded to Fraser River.

On 23 March 2025, the landing craft "C37202BC" known as "FULL TILT", with 4 people on board, reported being grounded on Snake Island, BC after fouling its propeller. The landing craft was removed from the environment with assistance from a commercial towing vessel. Damage to the landing craft hull was reported.

On 03 March 2025, the bulk carrier "EASTERN HAWK", reported that a stevedore was injured while performing cargo operations in the Port of Trois-Rivières, QC. The injured stevedore was transported to the local hospital by ambulance.

On 24 March 2025, the tanker "SILVER HANNAH", under the conduct of a pilot, reported being disabled due to electronics problem while approaching Vancouver Airport Fuel Delivery facility in Fraser River, BC.  The crew members carried out repairs and the vessel berthed safely.

On 23 March 2025, the bulk carrier "GOLDEN FREEZE", reported a failure of its main engine while transiting in the Gulf of St. Lawrence south of Anticosti Island, QC. The crew carried out the repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage.

On 21 March 2025, the bulk carrier "NUKUMI", reported having sustained a minor electrical fire in its engine room while proceeding in the Port of Montreal, QC. The crew extinguished the fire and the vessel continued its voyage.

On 20 March 2025, the tug "SST GRIZZLY", while transiting the Second Narrow Rail bridge in Vancouver, BC during flood tide, reported the tug's mast came into contact with the rail bridge. The rail bridge was in the process of opening for transit. After it was completely lifted, the tug resumed its voyage. Minor damage to the tug's equipment on the mast were reported.

On 19 March 2025, the tug "SEASPAN PROTECTOR", with the empty chip barge "SEASPAN 542" and the loaded paper barge "SMS 2" in tow, reported shutting down its starboard main engine due to overheating while transiting off Crown Island in Fraser River, BC. The "SEASPAN PROTECTOR" handed off the barges to the "SEASPAN VENTURE' and proceeded to a maintenance facility in Delta, BC. for repairs.

On 17 March 2025, the passenger vessel "CYQUABUS III", with 8 people on board, reported having struck its bow against a wharf while berthing in Granville Island, BC. One passenger sustained a serious injury and was sent to a hospital by ambulance once the vessel was secured. Minor damages to the bow were assessed.

On 16 March 2025, the fishing vessel "COLBY PERCE" with 6 persons on board reported having had an unexpected shutdown of the main engine. The vessel went to anchor and was able to effect repairs and continue on to Meteghan N.S.

On 16 March 2025, the fishing vessel "ARNOLD EDWARD" with 3 persons onboard, began taking on water.  The Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY" responded but the fishing vessel made it to Yarmouth N.S. unassisted.

On 14 March 2025, the crude oil tanker "NEW ARGOSY", while under the conduct of a pilot, reported having sustained a main engine failure in English Bay, BC. The vessel was assisted to Anchorage B in Vancouver Harbour, BC by the tugs "SAAM SABA" and "SAAM VOLTA".

On 10 March 2025, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CAPT JACQUES CARTIER" reported having sustained a total loss of propulsion 81 nm SSW of Cape Sable, NS, in the Gulf of Maine. The crew addressed the issue and the vessel resumed its voyage.

On 10 February 2025, the workboat "C20435ON", belonging to the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "PRIVATE ROBERTSON", reported having made bottom contact in the vicinity of the East Point Gut, NS. There were 4 people on board the workboat at the time. The workboat freed itself and returned to the "PRIVATE ROBERTSON" where the crew assessed the workboat for damage.

On 10 February 2025, the workboat "C20435ON", belonging to the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "PRIVATE ROBERTSON", reported having made bottom contact in the vicinity of the East Point Gut, NS. There were 4 people on board the workboat at the time. The workboat freed itself and returned to the "PRIVATE ROBERTSON" where the crew assessed the workboat for damage.

On 10 February 2025, the workboat "C20435ON", belonging to the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "PRIVATE ROBERTSON", reported having made bottom contact in the vicinity of the East Point Gut, NS. There were 4 people on board the workboat at the time. The workboat freed itself and returned to the "PRIVATE ROBERTSON" where the crew assessed the workboat for damage.

On 05 March 2025, the fishing vessel "JOSSY GIRL", with 4 people on board, reported being disabled with a total mechanical failure in St. Mary's Bay off Meteghan, NS. The vessel was towed to Freeport, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SAMBRO".
On 12 March 2025, the bulk carrier "TANJA" reported having sustained damage to its rudder caused by ice when departing the dock in Grande-Anse, QC. The vessel returned to the dock for repairs.

On 08 March 2025, the passenger ferry "NORTHERN ADVENTURE" reported an issue with one of its propellers while docked at the Bear Cove Ferry Terminal in Port Hardy, BC. The ferry cancelled its scheduled sailing to assess the problem and subsequently carried out repairs.

On 07 March 2025, the tug "SEASPAN CORSAIR", with 5 people on board, reported having run aground in the Fraser River off the Steveston Bar, BC. The vessel refloated at high tide without any assistance and proceeded to Annacis Island, BC.

On 07 March 2025, the fishing vessel "KORNAT I", with 3 people on board, reported having run aground in the Fraser River off the Steveston Bar, BC. The vessel refloated at high tide without any assistance and proceeded to a wharf in Steveston, BC.

On 07 March 2025, the general cargo vessel "BBC WISCONSIN" reported being beset in ice in the St. Lawrence River approximately 1 nautical mile upstream from the Quebec Bridge in Québec, QC. The Canadian Coast Guard vessel "VINCENT MASSEY" provided icebreaking assistance and the vessel resumed its voyage.

On 08 March 2025, the cargo vessel "RONJA ISLANDER", with 8 people on board, reported that it had struck a submerged rock and was taking on water in Tahsis Inlet, near Kendrick Camp, BC. The vessel proceeded to a dock in Gold River, BC, escorted by 2 other vessels. No injuries or pollution were reported.

On 06 March 2025, the container ship "CMA CGM PARANAGUA", sustained a failure of its steam system and had to stop off Anticosti Island, QC. The crew carried out the repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage.

On 06 March 2025, the container ship "MSC VERACRUZ", sustained a main engine failure prior its departure from berth 48 in the Port of Montreal, QC. The vessel remained moored for repairs then resumed its voyage.

On 06 March 2025, the fishing vessel "RYUO II", with 3 people on board, reported taking on water in the Comox harbor, near Comox Valley Marina, Comox, BC, due to a nonfunctional pump. The vessel proceeded to the marina and tied up safely, after which the pump became operational and successfully removed the water. The catch was transferred to another fishing vessel, and no injuries were reported.

On 05 March 2025, the general cargo ship "DAMGRACHT", reported being disabled as a result of a failure of its cooling system off Pointe-au-Père, QC. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage.

On 01 March 2025, the fishing vessel "GO CONG", with 2 people on board, reported being disabled and damaged after having collided with a floating log off Sand Heads in the Strait of Georgia, BC. The crew controlled a water ingress, and the vessel was towed to Steveston, BC by the Canadian Coast Guard hovercraft "MOYTEL" and by a local Royal Canadian Marine Search and Rescue workboat.

On 03 March 2025, the tug "H.M. SCOUT", with 2 people on board, reported running aground north of Tugboat Island, BC. The tug was freed without assistance and proceeded to Silva Bay, BC, under its own power.

On 05 March 2025, the fishing vessel "III KNOTTY BUOYS", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure off Sheet Harbour, NS. The vessel was towed to Sambro, NS, by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "HARE BAY".

On 24 February 2025, the fish carrier "INTER VIKING", with 5 persons onboard made bottom contact shortly after leaving the wharf in Harbour Breton, NL. The vessel returned to Harbour Breton, NL to assess the damages. Later the vessel proceeded to North Sydney, NS for docking and repairs.

On 03 March 2025, the asphalt/bitumen tanker "ATLANTIC ASPHALT", sustained a failure of its cooling system and was disabled off Île Blanche, QC. The crew carried out repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage.

On 02 March 2025, the crude oil tanker "LAURENTIA DESGAGNES", sustained a failure of its steering gear while leaving the anchorage in Trois-Rivières, QC. The vessel re-anchored for further investigations.

On 03 September 2024, the fishing vessel "EASTERN LADY", with 3 persons onboard had an injury onboard which lead to incapacitation. The crew returned to Pointe-Sapin, NB with the incapacitated crew member where an ambulance attended the injured. The crew member later died.

On 28 February 2025, the Canadian coast guard vessel "CAPT JACQUES CARTIER", reported a collision with a contractor's trailer on the dock at Bedford Institute of Oceanography, NS. There was no apparent damage to either the vessel or the trailer.

On 01 March 2025, the bulk carrier "BELGUARDIAN", reported being disabled due to a main engine problem while transiting Juan de Fuca Straits, BC. The tug "LYNN MARIE" towed "BELGUARDIAN' to the Constance Bank anchorage no.3 where the crew members carried out repairs.

On 28 February 2025, the fishing vessel "CAPE ASHLEY", with 3 persons onboard caught fire at the wharf in Glace Bay, NS. The 3 persons were able to evacuate to the wharf and the Glace Bay fire department responded. The vessel sank at the wharf the next day.
On 09 February 2025, the container vessel "COSCO AUCKLAND", reported losing its port anchor while anchoring at anchorage no.4 in Constance Bank, BC.
On 27 February 2025, bulk carrier "FEDERAL SKYE" sustained a failure of its main engine and was disabled off Grosses-Roches, QC. The crew carried out the repairs and the vessel resumed its voyage.

On 27 February 2025, the TUG "MERCURY XVI", with the barge "WM 56" in tow, reported a collision with the pleasure craft known as "TOMAHAWK" off Jericho Beach in Vancouver, BC. The crew boat " MERCURY XVIII" towed the "TOMAHAWK" to Kitsilano Coast Guard base, Vancouver. Damage to the sailing vessel was reported.

On 27 February 2025, the fishing vessel "ISLAND ALLSTAR", with 3 persons onboard, reported being disabled due to loss of steering off Cape Sable, NS. The vessel was towed by the Canadian Coast Guard vessel "CHEDABUCTO BAY" to West Head, NS.
On 22 February 2025, the tug "SEA IMP XI" reported having sustained a total failure of its port engine in Northumberland Channel, BC. The vessel resumed its voyage using the remaining engine.

On 24 February 2025, the fishing vessel "KMKA VOYAGER I", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure off Pubnico, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 22 February 2025, the fishing vessel "NORTHERN ALLIANCE", with 11 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure off Sheet Harbour, NS. The crew addressed the issue while waiting for assistance, and the vessel proceeded to Halifax, NS on its own power.

On 20 February 2025, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "KOPIT HOPSON 1752" reported having sustained a fire during hot work in its engine room while secured in Dartmouth, NS. The fire was extinguished, and the crew assessed the damages.

On 23 February 2025, the cargo ship "MOUNT SEYMOUR", with 18 people onboard, reported a crew member being injured during testing of a submersible pump while the vessel was alongside at the Lynnterm no.1 berth in Vancouver, BC. The injured crew member was treated by paramedics before being taken to the hospital. He was released from the hospital later the same day.

On 14 February 2025, the Canadian Coast Guard service ship "CGE735", struck an underwater object and reported sustaining damage to both underwater drives resulting in the loss of power and subsequent bottom contact while operating near Prince Rupert Harbour. Canadian Coast Guard vessel "MCINTYRE BAY" provided a tow to Port Edward, BC, for the vessel to be repaired.

On 15 February 2025, the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "HENRY LARSEN" reported experiencing severe weather and heavy rolling that caused machinery issues and minor damage to the vessel off Wild Cove, NL. Seven crew members sustained minor injuries.

On 19 February 2025, the fishing vessel "WESTERN GAMBLER", with 4 people on board, reported running aground and being at risk of capsizing near the McLoughlin Bay Ferry Terminal in Bella Bella, BC. The Canadian Coast Guard vessel "CAPE FAREWELL" responded to the distress call and transported the crew members to Bella Bella. No injuries were reported.

On 16 February 2025, the passenger ferry "F.-A.-GAUTHIER" reported that it sustained and engine failure on its port side main engine off Matane, QC. The vessel proceeded to the wharf of Matane, QC for further investigation.
On 13 February 2025, the TUG "INDIAN LAKE" with 3 persons on board, became disabled due to a failed transmission.  The Tug "R.J. BALLOT" towed the vessel to the wharf in Corner Brook, NL.

On 15 February 2025, the oil tanker "NAVIGATOR COPERNICO", under the guidance of a pilot, reported having experiencing failure of 1 of its main engines, and the vessel was at a risk of striking the jetty while berthing at Pembina Terminal, Prince Rupert, BC. The vessel was able to berth safely, and the crew members subsequently carried out repairs.
On 14 February 2025, the fishing vessel "PACIFIC QUEST", with 3 persons on board, reported being disabled near Meares Island, BC. A vessel of opportunity towed the fishing vessel to Tofino, BC.

On 13 February 2025, the bulk carrier "KEN OH", with the guidance of a pilot, reported that 1 of its main engines had failed while departing Vancouver Terminal, BC. The vessel continued its voyage by using its remaining operational engine and proceeded to Anchorage X with the assistance of three escort tugs. Once anchored, the crew carried out necessary repairs.

On 13 February 2025, the bulk carrier "AMIS POWER", under the guidance of a pilot, reported experiencing issues with 1 of its main engines in the Vancouver Harbour, near Vancouver, BC. The vessel continued its voyage using its remaining operational engine and proceeded to Anchorage 14 with the assistance of 3 escort tugs. Once anchored, the crew carried out necessary repairs.

On 12 February 2025, the passenger ferry "ISLAND K'ULUT'A", reported having a temporary failure of both its propulsion and steering systems while departing Campbell River Ferry Terminal, BC. The vessel subsequently regained full functionality and proceeded to Quathiaski Cove Terminal, where it docked and disembarked all passengers. Following the unloading, the ferry was relocated to a nearby lay-by berth, where crew members conducted necessary repairs.

On 17 February 2025, the passenger ferry "ALPHONSE-DESJARDINS" sustained its port side main engine failure off Lévis, QC. The vessel was assisted by a tug and an icebreaker to berth 101 of the Port of Québec, QC.

On 16 February 2025, the FISHING VESSEL "SARAH ELIZABETH" with 2 persons onboard reported being disabled due to a rope in the propeller.  The vessel was towed to Sambro, N.S. by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "HARE BAY".

On 15 February 2025, the CARGO VESSEL "MSC BALTIC III" with 20 persons onboard, sustained a blackout approximately 9.93 miles West of Little Port Head, NL and ran aground in Wild Cove, NL. The 20 persons were airlifted from the vessel and transported to the airport in Deer Lake, NL.  by a RCAF Cormorant Helicopter. 8 persons were transported to hospital in Corner Brook, NL and 4 were hospitalized.

On 10 February 2025, the tanker "NORDPENGUIN", under the conduct of a pilot, reported being struck by the escort tug "OCEAN GEORGIE BAIN" while departing Westridge Terminal, BC.  Minor damage to the tanker hull structure above the waterline was reported.

On 11 February 2025, the bulker "LILA CASABLANCA", under the conduct of a pilot, reported a total failure of its astern propulsion while shifting from anchorage "X" in Vancouver inner harbour to Alliance Grain terminal, Vancouver, BC.

On 12 February 2025, the ferry "ISLAND K'ULUT'A" reported having sustained a brief loss of propulsion and steering control while departing Campbell River, BC. The vessel proceeded to Quathiaski Cove, BC where the crew investigated the cause of the malfunction.

On 12 February 2025, the container ship "SEASPAN FALCON" reported having sustained damages to its main mast and communication equipment after being struck by a shore crane in Delta, BC. The crew assessed the damages and an inspection was scheduled.

On 28 January 2025, the tug "W. PEARCE", with the barge "ASPIRATION" on tow, reported making contact with the barge in Prince Rupert harbour. BC, while the master was maneuvering the tug to free up a bridle. The bridle was caught in the tug's stern rubber when the tug was shortening up to the barge. Major damage to the tug's wheelhouse and trunk cabin was reported.

On 12 February 2025, the fishing vessel "ROBERT ET CHANTAL", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a fouled propeller off Pubnico, NS. The vessel was towed to Ledge harbour, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 11 February 2025, the fishing vessel "MARITIME HARVESTER", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a total mechanical failure off Shelburne, NS. The vessel was towed to Port La Tour, NS by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 06 February 2025, the fishing vessel "PARKER & COLE", with 4 people on board, reported being disabled with a water ingress in the engine room in the vicinity of Sable Island, NS. The crew found a breach in the hull, and the bilge pumps were not sufficient to control the ingress. All crew members, wearing immersion suits, abandoned the sinking vessel and boarded the fishing vessel "FOUR LADIES", that proceeded to Louisbourg, NS.

On 06 February 2025, the fishing vessel "TRENT 'N' GIRLS", with 3 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure in the Gulf of Maine off Yarmouth, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "SAMBRO".
On 06 February 2025, the fishing vessel "ISLAND ALLSTAR", with 3 people on board, reported having fouled its propeller off West Head, NS. The vessel proceeded to the harbour at a reduced speed.

On 06 February 2025, the fishing vessel "HURTIN' UNIT", with 2 people on board, reported being disabled with a total engine failure off Sambro, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship ''HARE BAY".

On 05 February 2025, the fishing vessel "KNOT FOR SHORE", with 4 people on board, reported being disabled with a fouled propeller in the Gulf of Maine off Pubnico, NS. The vessel was towed into the harbour by the Canadian Coast Guard Ship "CHEDABUCTO BAY".

On 10 February 2025, the cargo vessel "SMOKE" reported having sustained an engine failure in the St. Lawrence River off Sept-Îles, QC. The crew assessed the issue, and the vessel proceeded to a nearby anchorage for repairs.
On 07 February 2025, the fishing vessel "FORTUNE PRIDE", with 4 people on board, sank off Sambro, NS. The crew abandoned the vessel. All crew members were recovered; two were pronounced deceased.
On 07 February 2025, the fishing vessel "FORTUNE PRIDE", with 4 people on board, sank off Sambro, NS. The crew abandoned the vessel. All crew members were recovered; two were pronounced deceased.

On 05 February 2025, the bulk carrier "UBC TACOMA", while under the conduct of a pilot, reported issues with its sea water cooling system in the St. Lawrence River off Lévis, QC. The vessel was secured to section No. 108 in Québec, QC to investigate the issue.

On 05 February 2025, the bulk carrier "LAMPARD", while under the conduct of a pilot, reported having sustained an engine failure in the Strait of Georgia, BC. The vessel proceeded to the inshore traffic zone where the engine was stopped for repairs, and once effected, resumed its voyage.

On 30 January 2025, the environmental response vessel "STRAIT SENTINEL", with 3 people on board, reported having sustained a main engine fire while preparing for departure from Beecher Bay, BC. The crew extinguished the fire and assessed the damages.

On 04 February 2025, the FISHING VESSEL "KNOTTY HABITS", located 59 nm ENE of Scatarie Island, N.S. reported that a crew member was injured while hauling fishing gear, the fishing vessel proceeded to Glace Bay, N.S. where the crew member was transported to hospital, treated and then released.

On 02 February 2025, the general cargo vessel "DIAMANTGRACHT", while under the conduct of a pilot, reported having sustained a total failure of its main engine cooling system and lost propulsion while approaching the Québec, QC pilot station. The vessel was secured to section 107 of Québec harbour by the tugs "OCEAN K. RUSB"Y and "OCEAN REYNALD T"; the crew effected repairs.

On 02 February 2025, the passenger ferry "QUEEN OF CAPILANO", with 34 people on board, reported making contact with a wooden dock structure and moored pleasure craft while departing the ferry terminal at Snug Cove on Bowen Island, BC. At the time, there were wind gusts and the ferry was experiencing issues with the controls for its azimuth thrusters. The controls were subsequently repaired.

On 29 January 2025, the container vessel "MSC ANGELA" reported that during cargo operations in the Port of Montreal, containers fell onto the vessel's deck and the pier. Cargo operations were stopped while the crew checked for damage to the vessel. The fallen containers were removed from the vessel and pier, and the vessel resumed cargo operations.
